title: Boss: INC-5532, delivered parcels flip back to shipped
summary: Find the keys the two producers disagree on, list the keys the partition increase moved, detect the out-of-order events, and build a reorder buffer that applies every order's events in version order.

steps.title: INC-5532: tracking page shows "shipped" after "delivered"
body: **INC-5532** · Sev 3 · Service: tracking-projector · Reporter: customer support (41 tickets this week)
> Customers see their parcel go **delivered → shipped** again. Refreshing later sometimes fixes it, sometimes not.
- topic shipment-events, keyed by orderId, grown from 6 to 8 partitions last Tuesday (kafka-topics.sh --alter)
- two producers: orders-api (C#, Confluent.Kafka, default Partitioner) and courier-gateway (Java, default partitioner)
- tracking-projector consumes with 4 replicas and applies every event as "status := event.status"
- every event carries the order's version (1, 2, 3, ...) since last year; the projector ignores it
02:14:07.112 apply A1 v3 delivered   partition=5 offset=88121
02:14:07.118 apply A1 v2 shipped     partition=3 offset=40377
1. List every record that sits on a different partition than the Java partitioner would choose, and every key the
2. Detect out-of-order and duplicate events in the projector's log (step 2).
3. The projector applies each order's events in version order: early events wait for the missing one, stale ones are
dropped, and a gap that never fills cannot block an order forever (step 3).

steps.title: 1. Which records are on the wrong partition?
prompt: `Murmur2` is given. Write three methods:
- `int PartitionFor(string key, int partitions)`: the Java client's partitioner,
`(Murmur2(UTF-8 bytes) & 0x7fffffff) % partitions`.
- `List<string> Misplaced(List<(string Key, int Partition)> observed, int partitions)`: for every observed record (in
input order) whose partition differs from `PartitionFor`, the line `"{key}: on p{observed}, Java expects p{expected}"`.
- `List<string> MovedKeys(IEnumerable<string> keys, int from, int to)`: for every key (in input order) whose partition
changes when the topic grows from `from` to `to` partitions, the line `"{key}: p{old} -> p{new}"`.

List<string> Misplaced(List<(string Key, int Partition)> observed, int partitions)
List<string> MovedKeys(IEnumerable<string> keys, int from, int to)

List<string> Misplaced(List<(string Key, int Partition)> observed, int partitions)
if (p != expected) result.Add($"{key}: on p{p}, Java expects p{expected}");
List<string> MovedKeys(IEnumerable<string> keys, int from, int to)
int a = PartitionFor(key, from), b = PartitionFor(key, to);

Deconstruct the tuples in a `foreach (var (key, p) in observed)` loop.

Dojo.Eq("correctly placed records pass", new List<string>(), Misplaced(new List<(string Key, int Partition)> { ("A1", 3) }, 8));
Dojo.Eq("no change, no moves", new List<string>(), MovedKeys(dojoKeys, 8, 8));

steps.title: 2. Spot the out-of-order events
prompt: Write `List<string> Violations(List<(string Key, long Version)> processed)` that reads the projector's log (in processing order) and reports, in order:
- a version **lower** than the highest version already processed for that key → `"{key}: v{version} after v{highest}"`;
- the **same** version as the highest already processed → `"{key}: v{version} again"`.
Versions that go up (even with gaps) are fine.
starter: List<string> Violations(List<(string Key, long Version)> processed)
solution: List<string> Violations(List<(string Key, long Version)> processed)
if (version < h) { result.Add($"{key}: v{version} after v{h}"); continue; }
if (version == h) { result.Add($"{key}: v{version} again"); continue; }
hints: Keep the highest version per key; compare before updating it.
A stale or duplicate event must not lower the stored highest version.
template: Dojo.Eq("the incident log", new List<string> { "A1: v2 after v3", "B7: v2 again", "A1: v1 after v4" }, Violations(dojoLog));
Dojo.Eq("gaps alone are not violations", new List<string>(), Violations(new List<(string Key, long Version)> { ("A1", 1), ("A1", 5), ("A1", 9) }));
Dojo.Eq("empty log", new List<string>(), Violations(new List<(string Key, long Version)>()));

steps.title: 3. A reorder buffer with a gap limit
prompt: Fix the projector: apply each order's events strictly in version order.
Write a class `ReorderBuffer`:
- `ReorderBuffer(int maxWaiting)`: at most `maxWaiting` events may wait per key.
- `List<string> Offer(string key, long version, string status)` returns what is applied **now**, as
`"{key} v{version} {status}"` lines (versions start at 1 per key):
- `version <= ` the last applied version: stale or duplicate, dropped, returns nothing;
- otherwise the event waits in the key's buffer (a second copy of a waiting version replaces it);
- if more than `maxWaiting` events now wait for this key and the lowest waiting version is not the next one, give up on the gap: add the line
`"{key} gap v{a} skipped"` (one missing version) or `"{key} gap v{a}..v{b} skipped"` (several), and continue as if
the last applied version were just below the lowest waiting one;
- then apply waiting events while the next version (`last + 1`) is there.
- `long Version(string key)`: last applied version (0 for unknown keys).
- `int Waiting`: how many events wait, over all keys.
starter: public List<string> Offer(string key, long version, string status) => new();
solution: readonly Dictionary<string, SortedDictionary<long, string>> waiting = new();
public List<string> Offer(string key, long version, string status)
if (!waiting.TryGetValue(key, out var w)) waiting[key] = w = new SortedDictionary<long, string>();
result.Add(from == to ? $"{key} gap v{from} skipped" : $"{key} gap v{from}..v{to} skipped");
hints: Per key keep the last applied version and a `SortedDictionary<long, string>` of waiting events.
After adding, if the buffer is too big, jump `last` to `lowestWaiting - 1` and report the skipped range.
Then loop `while (w.TryGetValue(last + 1, out var s))`, applying and removing.
template: Dojo.Eq("v1 applies at once", new List<string> { "A1 v1 packed" }, dojoR.Offer("A1", 1, "packed"));
Dojo.Eq("v3 waits for v2", new List<string>(), dojoR.Offer("A1", 3, "delivered"));
Dojo.Eq("the late v2 releases v3", new List<string> { "A1 v2 shipped", "A1 v3 delivered" }, dojoR.Offer("A1", 2, "shipped"));
Dojo.Eq("a duplicate v2 is dropped: delivered stays", new List<string>(), dojoR.Offer("A1", 2, "shipped"));
Dojo.Eq("B7 v2 waits", new List<string>(), dojoR.Offer("B7", 2, "packed"));
Dojo.Eq("B7 v3 waits", new List<string>(), dojoR.Offer("B7", 3, "shipped"));
Dojo.Eq("a third waiting event gives up on v1", new List<string> { "B7 gap v1 skipped", "B7 v2 packed", "B7 v3 shipped", "B7 v4 delivered" }, dojoR.Offer("B7", 4, "delivered"));
Dojo.Eq("a wider gap is reported as a range", new List<string> { "C4 gap v1..v3 skipped", "C4 v4 a" }, dojoWide.Offer("C4", 6, "b"));
Dojo.Eq("v6 still waits for v5", 1, dojoWide.Waiting);
Dojo.Eq("v5 releases v6", new List<string> { "C4 v5 c", "C4 v6 b" }, dojoWide.Offer("C4", 5, "c"));
